content: Each interaction is described in a clear and precise manner: 1. Lopinavir and Strong CYP3A4 Inhibitors: When co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, monitor closely as lopinavir increases the levels of seladelpar by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor for adverse effects. 2. Lopinavir and Seladelpar: Lopinavir increases seladelpar levels through mechanisms beyond CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for adverse effects, especially when co-administered with BCRP inhibitors. 3. Lopinavir and Selexipag: Lopinavir increases selexipag levels by reducing its metabolism. Although the clinical significance is uncertain, monitor closely. Co-administration with ritonavir may increase selexipag exposure, but this interaction is likely of minimal clinical importance. 4. Lopinavir and Selpercatinib: Lopinavir increases the toxicity of selpercatinib by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Lopinavir also increases selpercatinib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. 5. Lopinavir and Sertraline: Lopinavir increases sertraline levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, so avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 6. Lopinavir and Sevoflurane: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 7. Lopinavir and Sildenafil: Lopinavir increases sildenafil levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 8. Lopinavir and Simvastatin: Lopinavir significantly increases simvastatin levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism, leading to an increased risk of rhabdomyolysis. Co-administration is contraindicated. 9. Lopinavir and Siponimod: Lopinavir increases siponimod levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 10. Lopinavir and Sirolimus: Lopinavir increases sirolimus levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 11. Lopinavir and Sitagliptin: Lopinavir decreases the effects of sitagliptin through mechanisms other than CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Reports of hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance with protease inhibitors should be considered. 12. Lopinavir and Magnesium Sulfate/Potassium Chloride: These agents increase lopinavir toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Consider preand post-colonoscopy ECGs in patients at risk of serious cardiac arrhythmias. 13. Lopinavir and Sodium Sulfate/Potassium Sulfate/Magnesium Sulfate: These agents increase lopinavir toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Preand post-colonoscopy ECGs are recommended for at-risk patients. 14. Lopinavir and Solifenacin: Lopinavir increases solifenacin levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 15. Lopinavir and Sonidegib: Lopinavir increases sonidegib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 16. Lopinavir and Sorafenib: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Lopinavir also increases sorafenib levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. 17. Lopinavir and Sparsentan: Co-administration increases the toxicity of both drugs due to pharmacodynamic synergy. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, interrupt sparsentan treatment and consider dose titration upon resumption. 18. Lopinavir and St. John’s Wort: St. John’s Wort decreases lopinavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 19. Lopinavir and Stiripentol: Lopinavir increases stiripentol levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Stiripentol is both a CYP3A4 inhibitor and inducer. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Monitor CYP3A4 substrates for altered effects. 20. Lopinavir and Sufentanil: Lopinavir increases sufentanil levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase sufentanil plasma concentrations, potentially leading to fatal respiratory depression. 21. Lopinavir and Sunitinib: Lopinavir increases sunitinib levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 22. Lopinavir and Suvorexant: Lopinavir increases suvorexant levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is not recommended with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 23. Lopinavir and Tacrolimus: Lopinavir increases tacrolimus levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 24. Lopinavir and Talazoparib: Lopinavir increases talazoparib levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (P-gp) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Lopinavir and Tamoxifen: Lopinavir decreases tamoxifen metabolism to its active metabolite by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 26. Lopinavir and Tamsulosin: Lopinavir increases tamsulosin levels by altering CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug due to potential toxicity. 27. Lopinavir and Tasimelteon: Lopinavir increases tasimelteon levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Lopinavir and Tazemetostat: Lopinavir increases tazemetostat levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 29. Lopinavir and Tecovirimat: Tecovirimat decreases lopinavir levels by weakly inducing CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Lopinavir and Temsirolimus: Lopinavir increases temsirolimus levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 31. Lopinavir and Terbinafine: Lopinavir increases terbinafine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Lopinavir and Tetrabenazine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 33. Lopinavir and Tezacaftor: Lopinavir increases tezacaftor levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust the tezacaftor dosage regimen if co-administered with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. 34. Lopinavir and Tiagabine: Lopinavir increases tiagabine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 35. Lopinavir and Ticagrelor: Lopinavir increases ticagrelor levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid use with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 36. Lopinavir and Timolol: Lopinavir increases timolol levels by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely due to the risk of PR prolongation and cardiac arrhythmias. 37. Lopinavir and Tinidazole: Lopinavir increases tinidazole levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of toxicity. 38. Lopinavir and Tipranavir: Lopinavir increases tipranavir levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 39. Lopinavir and Tisotumab Vedotin: Lopinavir increases tisotumab vedotin levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Lopinavir and Tofacitinib: Lopinavir increases tofacitinib levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the tofacitinib dose to 5 mg daily when co-administered with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors. 41. Lopinavir and Tolterodine: Lopinavir increases tolterodine levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 42. Lopinavir and Tolvaptan: Lopinavir increases tolvaptan levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 43. Lopinavir and Topiramate: Topiramate decreases lopinavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Lopinavir and Topotecan: Lopinavir increases topotecan levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (P-gp). Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 45. Lopinavir and Toremifene: Lopinavir increases toremifene levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Lopinavir and Trabectedin: Lopinavir increases trabectedin levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 47. Lopinavir and Tramadol: Lopinavir increases tramadol levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Lopinavir and Trazodone: Lopinavir increases trazodone levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 49. Lopinavir and Triazolam: Lopinavir increases triazolam levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 50. Lopinavir and Triclabendazole: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 51. Lopinavir and Trimethoprim: Lopinavir increases trimethoprim levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 52. Lopinavir and Trimipramine: Lopinavir increases trimipramine levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 53. Lopinavir and Triptorelin: Triptorelin increases lopinavir toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 54. Lopinavir and Tucatinib: Tucatinib increases lopinavir levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 55. Lopinavir and Ubrogepant: Lopinavir increases ubrogepant levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 56. Lopinavir and Ulipristal: Lopinavir increases ulipristal levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 57. Lopinavir and Umeclidinium Bromide/Vilanterol: Lopinavir increases umeclidinium bromide/vilanterol levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 58. Lopinavir and Upadacitinib: Lopinavir increases upadacitinib levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 59. Lopinavir and Valbenazine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Lopinavir increases valbenazine levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust the valbenazine dose to 40 mg daily if co-administered.
